conviction_note: Near non-result: the CIB lines were pre-guided on 2026-09-15 and the card book is inside its guide. The one lever not in the wire is a likely NII guide lift after the 2026-09-16 Fed hike. It is partly offset by a 10y yield near 5% weighing on AOCI/CET1 and by a reaction history that sells beats (1 up in 4, Oct-2025 NII raise -1.9%), so findings sum to +0.5 and the scaled number is +0.2 (p_up 53 x abs 3.3).
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $5.86-5.91, revenue $50.85-51.15bn, from two agreeing estimate sources: https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/jpmorgan-q3-2026-earnings-preview-revenue-guidance-outlook ($5.86 / $50,847M, 2026-09-28) and https://www.marketpulse.com/markets/jpmorgan-q3-earnings-preview-can-strong-banking-momentum-continue/ ($5.91 / $51.15bn, 2026-10-07). Company guide FY26 NII ~$105.5bn, ex-Markets ~$96.5bn, adjusted expense ~$107.5bn, card NCO ~3.2%. Against H1 actuals (Q1 $25.4bn per 10-Q, Q2 $25.6bn) that implies ~$54.5bn of H2 NII. CIB pre-guide: IB fees and Markets revenue each +mid-to-high teens YoY.
positioning_check: Short interest 24.1m shares = 0.9% of shares outstanding, 2.57 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (equibles.com/stocks/jpm/shortinterest, read 2026-10-12, via sweep row). Not crowded. Skew_25d +1.88 vol points, a mild put bid; priced_direction_lean 'balanced'; put/call OI 0.55. Stock is -4.54% over 20d and -8.47% from its 52w high ($366.50 on 2026-08-13 per MarketPulse). RSI hit 31.6 on 2026-09-30. Event-implied move 3.03% (straddle 3.34%).

findings.finding: The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, with the SEP median pointing to one more hike by year-end. The July FY26 NII guide (~$105.5bn total, ~$96.5bn ex-Markets) was set before that. An asset-sensitive JPM is more likely to lift or firm the NII guide than to cut it, and NII is the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-14: NII guide raised to ~$105.5bn and the stock rose +2.5% (sweep row, marketbeat). 2025-10-14: NII forecast lifted with a profit beat and the stock fell -1.91% (baseline; bnnbloomberg.ca 2025/10/14 headline). A raise has been paid once and sold once.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector has traded rising rates as a negative: JPM fell 3.4% on 2026-09-23 as the 10y passed 5% and on 'broad de-risking' (247wallst 2026-09-22). The stock sits 8.5% below its August high. Had the market priced an NII raise as a positive, JPM would not have led the big-bank decline on the yield spike. The guide also needs H2 NII of ~$54.5bn against $51.0bn in H1, so the street has to take the ramp on trust until the call.
findings.independence: Proxy, not confirmed by the company: no mid-quarter NII comment from JPM was found. The Fed H.8 release of 2026-10-02 shows all-bank deposits +3.1%/+8.1% annualised in Jul/Aug and loans +3.8%/+9.0%, which supports the deposit-driven NII path (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h8/20261002/). Card revolving growth slowed to +2.3%/+0.4%, a small offset. H1 NII is from the Q1 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026029344/jpm-20260331.htm) and MarketPulse.

findings.finding: The 10y Treasury passed 5% in late September (highest since 2007) and the 10y-2y spread flattened to ~0.2%. That marks down AFS securities through AOCI, which counts in JPM's CET1, so CET1 and the buyback pace reported for Q3 are at risk of disappointing against Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved JPM reaction to a CET1/AOCI surprise in the baseline's four prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sector sell-off on the yield spike already reflects it, which is why the size is small. If it were fully priced, the call's CET1 number would carry no surprise. Nobody has published a quantified AOCI hit for JPM's Q3.
findings.independence: Inference: the AOCI-to-CET1 transmission is not quantified by JPM or any counterparty. The yield level is corroborated by the same-week report that JPM closed -3.42% at $340.51 on 2026-09-23 as the 10y passed 5% (easternherald.com/2026/09/24/..., 403 to fetch, snippet only).

findings.finding: JPM pre-guided Q3 IB fees and Markets revenue each up mid-to-high teens YoY on 2026-09-15, while BofA guided industry IB fees down ~10% and its own trading flat. LSEG's nine-month data imply Q3 global fees fell 19% q/q, roughly +2% YoY by arithmetic on the H1 and 9M totals. The industry series are softer than JPM's guide, which puts the low end of the guide at slight risk; late-September rate volatility is a slight upside for FICC.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 Markets revenue was a record (+35%) and IB +30%; the stock rose +2.5% but on the NII raise. The 2026-09-15 pre-guide itself moved the stock about +0.7-1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is wire copy and is priced; this finding lands inside what the company guided, so it is sized near 0. The only unpriced part is the gap to the industry series, and it would show as consensus IB/Markets estimates sitting below the guided growth, which no preview reports.
findings.independence: Dealogic (2026-10-07) ranks JPM #1 with $8.4bn of 9M26 fees and global 9M +16%, so JPM is taking share, which argues the guide holds (https://ionanalytics.com/insights/dealogic/investment-bankers-pocket-almost-usd-100bn-revenues-as-deal-making-soars-revenue-report/). LSEG figures via https://www.investmentexecutive.com/news/markets/strong-markets-boost-bankers-fortunes/; BofA via https://www.sharecafe.com.au/2026/09/15/bank-of-america-flags-investment-banking-fee-dip/.

findings.finding: JPM's own Chase Issuance Trust shows card credit benign into Q3: net credit losses 1.58% (Jul-26) and 1.66% (Aug-26) against 1.54% and 1.78% a year earlier, and total delinquency 0.81%/0.80% against 0.86%/0.83%. That fits under the lowered ~3.2% FY card NCO guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-01-13: -4.19% on a print carrying a $2.2bn Apple-card provision (finviz 2026-01-14). Credit surprises have moved this name; a benign in-guide quarter has not.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced and inside the guide, hence +0.1. The trust is a seasoned-prime subset of the card book, so the sell-side does not quote it. JPM analysts' price-target cuts on SYF, OMF and SLM on 2026-10-12 show consumer-credit worry is still in the air; if that were reconciled with JPM's own data, card NCO fears would not be weighing on the group.
findings.independence: Year-ago comparison from the Oct-2025 trust report (https://www.jpmorganchase.com/content/dam/jpmc/jpmorgan-chase-and-co/investor-relations/documents/asset-back-securities/chase-issuance-trust/chait-historical-trust-2025-10.pdf), which is the same issuer's series. Guide cut to 3.2% in July (hudson-labs preview). The trust is a narrow pool against a ~3.2% whole-book NCO, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: The bar into the print has been reset lower by the sector: JPM is 8.5% off its 2026-08-13 all-time high of $366.50 and -4.5% over 20 days, and it was oversold (RSI 31.6 on 2026-09-30) after BofA's 2026-09-14 fee warning took the bank index -2.7% and the yield spike. Short interest is not crowded and skew is only mildly put-bid.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's last four reactions are +2.50, -0.82, -4.19, -1.91: one up in four. This name has sold prints that went in near highs; this one goes in off them.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the pricing itself. The claim is only that JPM's own pre-guide (CIB up mid-to-high teens against BofA's down 10%) was lumped in with a sector de-rating. If JPM-specific strength were priced, JPM would not have fallen more than GS and BAC on 2026-09-22.
findings.independence: BofA-led sector drop: https://www.thewealthadvisor.com/article/bank-america-drops-5-after-brian-moynihan-warns-wall-street-fees-are-slowing. Shares the 247wallst document with finding 2 for the 2026-09-22 move; that is one fact used for different lines (capital vs positioning), not counted twice as the same claim.

outside_window.finding: The Apple Card portfolio purchase (>$20bn balances) is expected to close about 24 months after 2025-12-30, i.e. around early 2028. No Q3 2026 effect.

baseline_tension: Mildly against the baseline: the mild put skew (+1.88) and a 1-in-4 up reaction history lean down, while the findings lean slightly up on an NII-guide lift into a de-rated stock. The tension is small, so p_up is held at 53.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the NII-guide finding went from +0.6 to +0.4, because JPM sold the October 2025 NII raise (-1.9%) and paid only the July 2026 one (+2.5%).
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a proxy): the AOCI/CET1 finding went from -0.3 to -0.2, since JPM has not quantified it.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): two agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide were confirmed, so no cap was applied. Every finding resolves 2026-10-13. Apple Card was moved to outside_window.
Rule 1 on the fundamental read: print_vs_bar went from +1.0 to +0.8. The pre-guided CIB lines and an in-guide card book leave little room for a revenue surprise.
Left standing: the positioning finding at +0.3 (the skew is mild and short interest is 0.9%, so rule 7 does not bite), the credit finding at +0.1, abs_move_pct at 3.3 and p_up at 53.
